_description: Cartograph biology-priors domain file. Priors for scoring candidate SARS-CoV-2 viral–host PPI edges. Grounded in the Gordon et al. 2020 Nature AP-MS map (26 baits, 332 hi-confidence edges) enriched with human-human PPIs. Every PMID/DOI verified via NCBI E-utilities esummary + CrossRef.

_provenance.prey_source: prey_gene column of gordon2020_edges.csv (332 unique human preys)
_provenance.verification: All identifiers confirmed with NCBI E-utilities esummary (PubMed) and CrossRef works API on the date of assembly.

known_prey_complexes.name: NUP98–RAE1 mRNA export complex
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM: Nup98-Rae1; Reactome mRNA nuclear export
known_prey_complexes.relevance: Both are Orf6 prey and form an obligate heterodimer at the nuclear pore mediating mRNA export; SARS-CoV/CoV-2 Orf6 binds the RAE1–NUP98 interface to block nucleocytoplasmic transport and antagonize interferon. High-confidence anchor edge; a candidate touching one member strongly implies the other.

known_prey_complexes.name: Nuclear pore complex (nucleoporins)
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM/Reactome: Nuclear pore complex; NUP54/58/62 central FG-channel subcomplex
known_prey_complexes.relevance: Nsp9 prey are enriched for FG-nucleoporins (NUP54/58/62/88/214), Nsp4 additionally captured the transmembrane nucleoporin NUP210, and Orf6 captured NUP98/RAE1. Nucleoporins are strongly co-complexed; candidates within this set are prior-boosted, but note FG-nups are also known AP-MS sticky proteins (see false-positive patterns).

known_prey_complexes.name: HOPS / CORVET endolysosomal tethering complex
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM: HOPS complex (VPS11/16/18/33A/39/41); CORVET shares VPS11/16/18/33A core
known_prey_complexes.relevance: VPS11 (shared core) and VPS39 (HOPS-specific) are Orf3a prey. Full HOPS is a hexamer (VPS11/16/18/33A/39/41); only VPS11/VPS39 were captured here, so VPS16/VPS18/VPS33A/VPS41 are high-priority missing-edge candidates for Orf3a. Orf3a modulation of HOPS impairs autophagosome–lysosome fusion.

known_prey_complexes.name: Stress-granule G3BP nucleating core
known_prey_complexes.relevance: G3BP1 and G3BP2 are paralogous stress-granule nucleators and both N-protein prey. SARS-CoV-2 N binds G3BP1/2 to disassemble/sequester stress granules; other N prey (PABPC1/PABPC4, LARP1, MOV10, UPF1) are RNA-granule associated, so N candidates in this RNP set are prior-boosted.

known_prey_complexes.name: TOM/TIM mitochondrial protein-import machinery
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM: TIM9-TIM10 complex; Reactome mitochondrial protein import (TOM/TIM)
known_prey_complexes.relevance: TOMM70 (Orf9b) is the outer-membrane import receptor; the small TIM chaperones (TIMM9/10/10B/29, Nsp4 prey) form the intermembrane-space carrier pathway. Orf9b binds TOMM70 to suppress MAVS/interferon signaling. TOMM70 is a documented anchor edge.

known_prey_complexes.name: CRL2 Cullin-RING ubiquitin ligase (Elongin BC–CUL2–RBX1)
known_prey_complexes.relevance: All five are Orf10 prey and constitute a canonical CRL2 module: scaffold CUL2, RING RBX1, adaptor Elongin B/C (ELOB/ELOC), and substrate receptor ZYG11B. Any candidate contacting one CRL2 subunit implies the assembled ligase. (Note: the cited work reports the Orf10–CRL2 complex is dispensable for replication — evidence the interaction is real, biological effect debated.)

known_prey_complexes.name: RNA exosome (EXOSC ribonuclease core)
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM/Reactome: cytoplasmic and nuclear RNA exosome (9-subunit core EXOSC1-9)
known_prey_complexes.relevance: Four EXOSC subunits are Nsp8 prey. The exosome core is a 9-subunit barrel (EXOSC1–9); captured members EXOSC2/3/5/8 make EXOSC1/4/6/7/9 and the catalytic DIS3 high-priority missing-edge candidates.

known_prey_complexes.name: Signal recognition particle (SRP)
known_prey_complexes.relevance: SRP19, SRP54 (signal-peptide GTPase) and SRP72 are Nsp8 prey. Co-membership predicts remaining SRP subunits (SRP9/14/68) as candidates; couples to co-translational ER targeting.

known_prey_complexes.name: Casein kinase 2 (CK2) holoenzyme
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM: CK2 holoenzyme (two CSNK2A catalytic + two CSNK2B regulatory)
known_prey_complexes.relevance: CK2 is an α2β2 tetramer; catalytic CSNK2A2 and regulatory CSNK2B are both N-protein prey, so the paralog CSNK2A1 is a strong missing-edge candidate. N is a CK2 substrate and CK2 was flagged as a druggable node in Gordon et al.

known_prey_complexes.name: Adaptor protein complex 2 (AP-2, clathrin adaptor)
known_prey_complexes.corum_reactome: CORUM: AP-2 adaptor complex (AP2A1/A2, AP2B1, AP2M1, AP2S1)
known_prey_complexes.relevance: AP2A2 (alpha) and AP2M1 (mu) are Nsp10 prey; the AP-2 heterotetramer's remaining AP2B1/AP2S1 are candidate edges. Links to clathrin-mediated endocytosis.

known_prey_complexes.name: Mitochondrial processing peptidase (MPP) / matrix proteases
known_prey_complexes.relevance: PMPCA/PMPCB form the presequence-cleaving MPP heterodimer; both are M-protein prey (with matrix peptidase PITRM1), a coherent mitochondrial-matrix protease module.

known_prey_complexes.name: DNA polymerase alpha–primase
known_prey_complexes.relevance: All four subunits of the pol-α/primase heterotetramer are Nsp1 prey — an internally complete, high-coherence complex; strong intra-complex edge prior.

typical_interaction_types: N (nucleocapsid): RNA-binding proteins, stress-granule/RNP components (G3BP1/2, PABPC1/4, LARP1, MOV10, UPF1) and CK2 kinase — reflects genome packaging and phase-separation control.
M (membrane): ER/Golgi membrane proteins, mitochondrial import/matrix proteases (PMPC), vacuolar-ATPase and transporters — assembly/budding at ERGIC.
E (envelope): trafficking/scaffold adaptors (AP3B1), bromodomain proteins (BRD2/BRD4) — ion-channel/scaffolding roles.
Spike: Golgi-resident palmitoyl-transferase machinery (ZDHHC5, GOLGA7) — post-translational modification and trafficking of the glycoprotein.
structural_proteins.rationale: Structural proteins localize to membranes and RNP granules; expect enrichment for membrane-trafficking, lipid-modification, and RNA-binding partners rather than catalytic enzyme complexes.

typical_interaction_types: Replication-transcription complex components (Nsp7/8/9/10/12/13/14) engage RNA-processing and nucleic-acid machinery: DNA pol-α/primase (Nsp1), SRP and RNA exosome (Nsp8), nucleoporins (Nsp9), centrosome/Golgi structural proteins and PKA (Nsp13).
Nsp7: vesicular trafficking small GTPases (RAB1A/2A/5C/7A/8A/10/14/18, RHOA, RALA) — membrane remodeling for replication organelles.
Nsp13 (helicase): microtubule/centrosome and Golgi structural network plus PKA holoenzyme and TBK1 innate-immune kinase.
nonstructural_proteins_nsp.rationale: Nsps build the membrane-bound replication organelle and RNA-synthesis machinery; expect enzyme complexes, RNA-processing machines, cytoskeletal/centrosomal scaffolds, and innate-immune kinases. Interactions are often enzymatic-substrate or scaffolding rather than stable stoichiometric complexes.

typical_interaction_types: Immune antagonism and trafficking: Orf6→NUP98/RAE1 (nuclear export block); Orf9b→TOMM70 (MAVS/interferon suppression); Orf3a→HOPS (VPS11/VPS39, autophagy).

Secretory/ER-quality-control and glycosylation: Orf8→ER lumenal chaperones and glycosyltransferases (HYOU1, SDF2, EDEM3, FKBP7/10, POGLUT/POFUT); Orf9c→ER/mitochondrial membrane and OXPHOS-assembly factors (NDUFAF1, ECSIT, NLRX1).
accessory_orfs.rationale: Accessory ORFs are specialized host-antagonism effectors: expect discrete, mechanistically-focused targets in innate-immune, nucleocytoplasmic-transport, autophagy/endolysosomal, ubiquitin-ligase and ER-secretory pathways — often hijacking a defined host complex.

ap_ms_false_positive_patterns.description: Proteins that co-purify non-specifically across many unrelated baits (heat-shock/chaperones HSPA/HSPD, tubulins, actin, ribosomal proteins, translation factors, keratins, TCP1/CCT). The CRAPome quantifies how often each prey appears in negative/GFP controls; high-frequency preys should be down-weighted regardless of MiST/score.

Highly abundant cellular proteins yield spectral counts by mass action, not specific binding. Specificity-aware scores (SAINT, MiST, CompPASS) model prey abundance/reproducibility across controls; interactions not enriched over controls are probable false positives. Gordon et al. used MiST + SAINTexpress + PPI-scoring to filter, but residual abundant-protein bias remains.

Ribosomal subunits (RPL/RPS, MRPS), chaperones (HSP70/90, FKBP, prefoldin), and cytoskeletal proteins (tubulin/actin, keratin) are recurrent AP-MS background. A lone ribosomal or chaperone prey without co-complex partners should be treated as low-prior; enrichment of an entire coherent complex is more credible than a single sticky subunit.

Baits are epitope-tagged and over-expressed (here in HEK293T), which can force non-physiological interactions, mislocalize the bait, or expose surfaces that recruit spurious partners. Interactions should ideally be corroborated by orthogonal evidence (reciprocal pulldown, endogenous co-IP, structure, or independent screen) before high confidence.

ap_ms_false_positive_patterns.pattern: Indirect / co-complex membership vs direct binding
ap_ms_false_positive_patterns.description: AP-MS captures co-complex membership, not direct binary contact; a prey may associate through a bridging protein. For link prediction this inflates apparent direct-edge density within complexes. Treat within-complex edges as co-membership priors, not proof of direct interaction.
